TokenBatch::tokens¶

Back to TokenBatch API Reference

Signature¶

const Note& TokenBatch::tokens() const

Access The Flat Ragged Payload¶

tokens() returns the rank-one Note containing every emitted token in row-major source-cell order. It is the value half of TokenBatch; the offsets() Note supplies the row boundaries.

For normal text operations the payload uses NoteDType::Text. The closed TokenBatch contract also permits Bytes so byte-oriented producers can retain their dtype without converting arbitrary bytes to text. The payload is always rank one regardless of the source Note’s rank because ragged rows cannot be encoded as a rectangular multidimensional shape. Its length is offsets().integers().back().

No token content is copied by this accessor. It returns a borrowed const Note& owned by the TokenBatch implementation. That reference remains valid while a handle sharing the implementation remains alive. If independent lifetime is needed, copy the Note value:

pluss::Note retained = batch.tokens();

The copy is still cheap: Note is itself a reference-counted handle, so token bytes remain shared rather than duplicated.

A defined all-empty batch returns a defined rank-one Text Note with zero elements. A batch that propagates an undefined input returns an undefined token Note and canonical offsets [0]. Calling tokens() on a default-constructed undefined TokenBatch throws pluss::Error.

Example 1: Flat Tokens Preserve Source-Cell Order¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::note::make({"red green", "", "blue"}).nlp().tokens();
const auto& tokens = batch.tokens();

std::cout << "dtype=" << pluss::dtype_name(tokens.dtype())
          << " shape=[" << tokens.size(0) << "] values=[";
for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < tokens.numel(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << '"' << tokens.at(i) << '"';
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

dtype=Text shape=[3] values=["red", "green", "blue"]

The empty middle row emits no placeholder. Its location survives in the offsets, not in this flat Note.

Example 2: Pair Tokens With Their Boundaries¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::note::make({"red green", "", "blue"}).nlp().tokens();
const auto bounds = batch.offsets().integers();

for (std::size_t row = 0; row + 1 < bounds.size(); ++row) {
  std::cout << "row " << row << " count="
            << bounds[row + 1] - bounds[row] << '\n';
}

Output¶

row 0 count=2
row 1 count=0
row 2 count=1

Never infer rows from token text; offsets are the authoritative structure.

Example 3: A Defined Empty Payload¶

const auto batch = pluss::note::make({"", "!!!"}).nlp().tokens();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "batch-defined=" << batch.defined()
          << " tokens-defined=" << batch.tokens().defined()
          << " token-count=" << batch.tokens().numel() << '\n';

Output¶

batch-defined=true tokens-defined=true token-count=0

Example 4: Propagated Absence¶

const auto batch = pluss::Note::undefined().nlp().tokens();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "batch-defined=" << batch.defined()
          << " tokens-defined=" << batch.tokens().defined() << '\n';

Output¶

batch-defined=true tokens-defined=false

This is not the same state as Example 3.

Example 5: Retain The Payload Beyond One Handle¶

pluss::Note retained;
{
  const auto batch = pluss::note::make({"red green"}).nlp().tokens();
  retained = batch.tokens();
}
std::cout << retained.at(0) << ' ' << retained.at(1) << '\n';

Output¶

red green

Copying the returned Note handle keeps its storage alive after the local batch is destroyed.

Example 6: Undefined Handle Access Is Rejected¶

const pluss::TokenBatch batch;
try {
  (void)batch.tokens();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "default tokens: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

default tokens: rejected

See Also¶

  • offsets: recover the logical rows of this flat Note.

  • defined: test whether payload access is legal.

  • empty: test whether this Note has any token lanes.
